ALMA observations were obtained through two different projects (2017.1.01020.S and 2019.1.00862.S; PI: T. Bisbas): the first one provides low-resolution observations in band 4, while the second one is a high-resolution follow-up in both band 4 and band 3.

We study the dynamics of cold molecular gas in two main-sequence galaxies at cosmic noon (zC-488879 at $z\simeq1.47$ and zC-400569 at $z\simeq2.24$) using new high-resolution ALMA observations of multiple $^{12}$CO transitions.
To shed new light on galaxy dynamics at cosmic noon, we present an in-depth study of two galaxies with kinematic and photometric data of the highest quality.

ALMA observations were obtained through two different projects (2017.1.01020.S and 2019.1.00862.S; PI: T. Bisbas): the first one provides low-resolution observations in band 4, while the second one is a high-resolution follow-up in both band 4 and band 3.

In both bands, we used a mixed spectral setup with four spectral windows (SPWs) with a bandwidth of 1.875 GHz each.

All line SPWs were covered with 1920 channels giving a channel width of 4$-$5 $\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, while the continuum SPWs were covered with 128 channels giving a channel width of 60$-$100 $\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.

For band-4 observations, the four SPWs cover the CO($3-2$) line of zC-488879, the CO($4-3$) line of zC-400569, the \[C I\]($1-0$) line of zC-400569, and the 2-mm continuum.

and (4) Milgromian dynamics (MOND) can successfully fit the rotation curves with the same acceleration scale $a_0$ measured at $z\simeq0$.
This implies that rotation curves at $z\simeq1-2$ are compatible with the value of $a_0$ and the interpolation function measured at $z\simeq0$.

Nevertheless, the properties of these two high-$z$ galaxies (high $V_{\rm rot}/\sigma_{\rm V}$ ratios, inner rotation curve shapes, bulge-to-total mass ratios) are remarkably similar to those of massive spirals at $z\simeq0$, suggesting weak dynamical evolution over more than 10 Gyr of the Universe’s lifetime.

Despite all these limitations, Figure [10](#fig:SPARC) shows a remarkable fact: the inner rotation curves ($R<8-9$ kpc) of zC-400569 and zC-488879 are very similar to those of local galaxies with similar stellar surface densities ($\sim$10$^{3}$ M$_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$).
This galaxy is one of the best observed object from the SINS IFU survey (cite: Forster2009; Forster2018; Genzel2017).

Luckily, next to zC-400569, there is another main-sequence galaxy at $z=1.47$ (COSMOS 0488879 or COSMOS2015 0301356) so we set up our ALMA observations to simultaneously target the CO($2-1$) and CO($3-2$) lines of this second object (see Fig. [1](#fig:TwoBirds)).

In addition to getting observations with the highest possible spatial resolution, the best approach to account for beam-smearing effects is modeling the three-dimensional (3D) emission-line datacube in a nonparametric fashion (cite: Corbelli1997; Sicking1997; Swaters1999; Fraternali2001; Fraternali2002; Gentile2003; Gentile2004; Gentile2007; Jozsa2007; Swaters2009; Lelli2010; Lelli2012a; Lelli2012b; Lelli2014; DiTeodoro2015).
We model the gas kinematics in a nonparametric fashion without a-priori assumption on the gas density profile, rotation curve shape, and gravitational potential.
We explored the use of higher-order polynomials but they did not significantly improved the continuum subtraction.
The profiles from the F110W filter show a similar shape but they have larger errors, so they will not be used in the rest of this paper.

For zC-400569, the same model does not provide satisfactory results because the surface brightness profile displays a curvature at $1''<R<2''$ that is reminiscent of “lenses” and “barlenses” in disk galaxies at $z\simeq0$ (cite: Laurikainen2011; Athanassoula2015).
We were not able to perform a detailed kinematic analysis of the \[C I\] data, so we use them solely as a total H$_2$ mass tracer in Sect. [5.3](#sec:onlybaryons).

Parametric 3D models assume predefined functions for the rotation-curve shape and the gas density profile, so they necessarily make implicit assumptions on the intrinsic strength of beam-smearing effects.

For both galaxies the bulge parameters are very uncertain (especially $R_{\rm e,\,bul}$) because most of the bulge light is contained within the PSF ($\sim$0.15$''$ or $\sim$1.3 kpc for the adopted cosmology).
Most likely, the available spectral resolution ($\Delta_{\rm V}$), spatial resolution, and sensitivity do not allow us to robustly measure the intrinsic velocity dispersion.
Our computation of $V_{\rm gas}$ neglects the contribution of atomic gas (H I), which may dominate the total gas budget of high-$z$ galaxies (cite: Chowdhury2022).
As it is often the case in Astronomy, the errors $\delta_{V_{\rm rot}}$ are “educated guesses” and do not truly represent a strict 1$\sigma$ deviation from a Gaussian distribution.

The question of the amount and distribution of dark matter in high-$z$ galaxies remains unsettled due to the limited spatial extent of the available kinematic data; we discuss the suitability of various emission lines to trace extended rotation curves at high $z$.

all_quotes.quote: If we assume that the rotation curves of our high-$z$ galaxies remain flat at the observed values, then they should be traced out to $20-30$ kpc to unambiguougly probe the DM-dominated regime.
The SINFONI data of zC-400569 were obtained from the archive of the SINS/zC-SINF Adapative Optics (AO) survey[^1] (cite: Forster2018).

Since we aim to model the stellar mass distribution of these galaxies, we analyzed the reddest HST images available in the Hubble Legacy Archive[^2], which were taken with the NIR F160W and F110W filters of the Wide Field Camera 3 (WFC3; Project ID 12578).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA$\#$2017.1.01020.S and ADS/JAO.ALMA$\#$2019.1.00862.
